value.body: Resident doctors are junior or postgraduate doctors working in a hospital department under senior consultants. The day involves ward rounds, admitting and examining patients, ordering and reading tests, procedures, emergency duty and night shifts, along with study for the postgraduate course.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: MBBS, internship and NEET-PG for a postgraduate seat

items.label: Residency length
items.value: 3 years for MD / MS; 2 years for most diplomas

items.label: PG medical seats
items.note: MD / MS / DNB and diploma seats
items.source: Health Ministry reply in Parliament (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After MBBS and a one-year internship, doctors register with the NMC or a state council. Junior residencies without a PG seat (often called non-academic or senior house officer posts) are available in many hospitals; a postgraduate residency needs a NEET-PG rank and counselling.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Writing case notes and discharge summaries

value.title: At a glance
items: Duty hours are long, including nights and on-call shifts.
Common next steps: senior residency, super-specialty training, or consultant posts.
NEET-PG competition is high; many doctors take more than one attempt.
